items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: there’s been several things in JEN J- © Fillius Jazz Archive -13- E-N — Jazz Education Network — that I just actually wonder about

ctx.x: Well thank you for saying that because I think mistakes or unintended notes — it may depend on who you’re working with and what age. But I can see how Michael Brecker — people might write out, transcribe Michael Brecker’s solos and point out that look he played a major third over a minor chord, and they will justify it. They will say it’s a color tone or watch because he does it seven measures later. It’s a bit of a conundrum I think. I was debating about whether to do this or not and I’m going to give it a try…

Well that’s analysis and that’s the left side of the brain taking over. I don’t know — that sounds like something I’ve read before though, and there’s been several things in JEN J- © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

E-N — Jazz Education Network — that I just actually wonder about and I kind of wonder how can this be helpful to someone trying to play a blues or trying to play a tune. I don’t know. Maybe I’m still — maybe I’m still stuck back playing changes and maybe this person isn’t. I don’t know.
